subproblems.title: Support of a difference of currents
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P and all currents S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), the difference current S − T of the frozen contract (Sub instance, (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω)) satisfies spt(S − T) ⊆ spt S ∪ spt T. Here spt R = U ∖ Z(R) (GeometricCurrentOn.support). The zero region Z(R) is the union of all open sets W with closure(W) compact and closure(W) ⊆ U such that R(ω) = 0 for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (S - T).support ⊆ S.support ∪ T.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact 1(d) of the parent proof (spt(S − A) ⊆ spt S ∪ spt A), written for an arbitrary domain U.

Notation: R ∈ 𝒟_n(U) vanishes on W (GeometricCurrentOn.VanishesOn) if R(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. The zero region Z(R) (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion) is the union of all W such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and R vanishes on W. Then spt R = U ∖ Z(R).

1. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω). The Sub instance of the frozen contract sets the underlying linear functional of S − T to S.toCurrent − T.toCurrent, and (f − g)(ω) = f(ω) − g(ω) for linear maps (LinearMap.sub_apply; this holds by rfl).
2. Let y ∈ spt(S − T). Then y ∈ U and y ∉ Z(S − T). Suppose, for a contradiction, that y ∉ spt S and y ∉ spt T.
3. Since y ∈ U and y ∉ spt S = U ∖ Z(S), we have y ∈ Z(S). So there is an open W₁ with y ∈ W₁, closure W₁ compact, closure W₁ ⊆ U, and S vanishing on W₁. Likewise y ∈ Z(T) gives an open W₂ ∋ y with closure W₂ compact, closure W₂ ⊆ U, and T vanishing on W₂.
4. Put W := W₁ ∩ W₂. It is open as an intersection of two open sets, and it contains y. Since W ⊆ W₁, closure W ⊆ closure W₁ (closure_mono), hence closure W ⊆ U. Also closure W is compact, being a closed subset of the compact set closure W₁ (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset with isClosed_closure).
5. S − T vanishes on W. If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ and tsupport ω ⊆ W₂. Hence S(ω) = 0 and T(ω) = 0, and by step 1, (S − T)(ω) = 0 − 0 = 0.
6. By steps 4–5, W belongs to the family whose union is Z(S − T), so y ∈ W ⊆ Z(S − T). This contradicts step 2. Hence y ∈ spt S ∪ spt T, which proves spt(S − T) ⊆ spt S ∪ spt T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold spt R = U ∖ Z(R) and (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω).
A point y ∈ U outside spt S ∪ spt T lies in zero-region sets W₁ (for S) and W₂ (for T).
W₁ ∩ W₂ is open, contains y, has compact closure contained in U, and S − T vanishes on it.
Hence y ∈ Z(S − T), contradicting y ∈ spt(S − T).

subproblems.title: Subadditivity of local mass for a difference of currents
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all sets U, W ⊆ ℝ^P and all currents S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n): M_W(S − T) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T) in [0, ∞]. Here S − T is the difference current of the frozen contract, and M_W(R) = sup{ENNReal.ofReal(R(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn with massAdmissibleOn U n W), where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (S - T).massOn W ≤ S.massOn W + T.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact 1(c) of the parent proof (M(S − A) ≤ M(S) + M(A)), written for an arbitrary domain U and an arbitrary support region W.

Notation: a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) is W-admissible (ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W) if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is covectorEuclideanNorm. M_W(R) = sSup{ENNReal.ofReal(R(ω)) : ω W-admissible} (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn).

1. Since M_W(S − T) is defined as a supremum (sSup_le), it suffices to prove ENNReal.ofReal((S − T)(ω)) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T) for every W-admissible ω. Fix such an ω.
2. −ω is W-admissible. It lies in 𝒟^n(U) because test forms form a submodule. As a form it equals the pointwise negative −(ω : DifferentialForm) (the coercion of a submodule negation, by rfl). So tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω ⊆ W (tsupport_neg), and |(−ω)(x)| = |−(ω(x))| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
3. (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) − T(ω) by the definition of the Sub instance (LinearMap.sub_apply, rfl). Also T(−ω) = −T(ω) by linearity (T.toCurrent.map_neg ω). Hence (S − T)(ω) = S(ω) + T(−ω).
4. ENNReal.ofReal(S(ω) + T(−ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(S(ω)) + ENNReal.ofReal(T(−ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le).
5. GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, applied to the W-admissible forms ω and −ω, gives ENNReal.ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ M_W(S) and ENNReal.ofReal(T(−ω)) ≤ M_W(T).
6. Combining steps 3–5 with add_le_add gives ENNReal.ofReal((S − T)(ω)) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T). Taking the supremum over all W-admissible ω gives M_W(S − T) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one W-admissible ω by sSup_le.
−ω is W-admissible (tsupport_neg, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
(S − T)(ω) = S(ω) + T(−ω), and ENNReal.ofReal is subadditive.
Apply le_massOn to ω and −ω, then take the supremum.

subproblems.title: Mass of the current obtained by integrating over a ball
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let μ be a measure on ℝ^P. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n, the continuous linear functionals on Covector (Euclid P) n) satisfy |ξ(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. y and every α ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P), where |·| is covectorEuclideanNorm. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ, and let A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(y)(ω(y)) dμ(y) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), where B_ρ(x) is the open ball. Then M(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) in [0, ∞], where M(A) = A.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (x : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), (∀ᵐ y ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ y α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, A ω = ∫ y in ball x ρ, ξ y ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y) ∂μ) → A.mass ≤ μ (ball x ρ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the first half of fact 1(e) of the parent proof (M(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x))). The parent uses finiteness of μ(B_ρ(x)); here a trivial case distinction replaces it, so no local finiteness or measurability hypothesis is needed.

Notation: M(A) = A.mass = A.massOn univ = sSup{ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y}. The support condition tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P in massAdmissibleOn univ n univ is automatic.

1. If μ(B_ρ(x)) = ∞, then M(A) ≤ ∞ = μ(B_ρ(x)) (le_top). Assume from now on that μ(B_ρ(x)) ≠ ∞, so μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞.
2. Since M(A) is defined as a supremum (sSup_le), it suffices to show ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) for every ℝ^P-admissible ω, i.e. every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. Fix such an ω and write f(y) := ξ(y)(ω(y)) ∈ ℝ. By hypothesis, A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} f dμ.
3. For μ-a.e. y, the hypothesis on ξ with α := ω(y) gives |f(y)| = |ξ(y)(ω(y))| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1. A statement holding μ-a.e. also holds a.e. for the restriction μ⌞B_ρ(x) (ae_restrict_of_ae). So ‖f(y)‖ = |f(y)| ≤ 1 for μ⌞B_ρ(x)-a.e. y (Real.norm_eq_abs).
4. By norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const_ae (with s := B_ρ(x), μ(s) < ∞ and constant C := 1), |∫_{B_ρ(x)} f dμ| ≤ 1 · μ.real(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal. This lemma needs no measurability of f: if f is not a.e. strongly measurable, its Bochner integral is 0.
5. Hence A(ω) ≤ |A(ω)| ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal (le_abs_self). Therefore ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal) = μ(B_ρ(x)), by ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal (using μ(B_ρ(x)) ≠ ∞).
6. Taking the supremum over ω gives M(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)). ∎
proof_key_steps: The bound is trivial if μ(B_ρ(x)) = ∞.
For admissible ω, |ξ(y)(ω(y))| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for μ⌞B_ρ(x)-a.e. y.
norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const_ae gives A(ω) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal.
Apply ENNReal.ofReal and take the supremum: M(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)).

subproblems.title: Support of the current obtained by integrating over a ball
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be any measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) any function. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ, and let A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(y)(ω(y)) dμ(y) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), where B_ρ(x) is the open ball. Then spt A ⊆ B̄_ρ(x), the closed ball (spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (x : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, A ω = ∫ y in ball x ρ, ξ y ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y) ∂μ) → A.support ⊆ closedBall x ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the second half of fact 1(e) of the parent proof (spt A ⊆ B̄_ρ(x)).

Notation: A vanishes on W' if A(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W'. The zero region Z(A) is the union of all open W' with closure W' compact (and contained in ℝ^P, which is automatic) on which A vanishes. Then spt A = ℝ^P ∖ Z(A) (GeometricCurrentOn.support).

1. Let y ∈ spt A, so y ∉ Z(A). Suppose, for a contradiction, that y ∉ B̄_ρ(x), i.e. dist(y, x) > ρ. Put r := (dist(y, x) − ρ)/2 > 0 and W' := B_r(y).
2. W' is open (isOpen_ball) and y ∈ W' (mem_ball_self, since r > 0). Its closure lies in the closed ball B̄_r(y) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). That ball is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall), so closure W' is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset with isClosed_closure). Trivially closure W' ⊆ ℝ^P.
3. A vanishes on W'. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W', and let z ∈ B_ρ(x), so dist(z, x) < ρ. By the triangle inequality dist(y, x) ≤ dist(y, z) + dist(z, x), we get dist(z, y) = dist(y, z) ≥ dist(y, x) − dist(z, x) > dist(y, x) − ρ = 2r > r. Hence z ∉ W', so z ∉ tsupport ω and ω(z) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Since ξ(z) is linear, ξ(z)(ω(z)) = ξ(z)(0) = 0 (map_zero). So the integrand vanishes at every point of B_ρ(x), and A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(z)(ω(z)) dμ(z) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
4. By steps 2–3, W' belongs to the family whose union is Z(A), so y ∈ W' ⊆ Z(A). This contradicts step 1. Hence y ∈ B̄_ρ(x), i.e. spt A ⊆ B̄_ρ(x). If ρ ≤ 0, then B_ρ(x) = ∅ and the same argument applies verbatim. ∎
proof_key_steps: For y with dist(y, x) > ρ, take W' = B_r(y) with r = (dist(y, x) − ρ)/2 > 0.
W' is open, contains y and has compact closure.
Every test form supported in W' vanishes on B_ρ(x), so A vanishes on W'.
Hence y ∈ Z(A), so y ∉ spt A.

subproblems.title: Comparison estimate A(ω) ≤ (κ + cR(1+κ))·m from a small filling and the cone bound
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, A, S ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (d+1)), and ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P) with |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for every y (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm). Let m ∈ [0, ∞] with m < ∞, x ∈ ℝ^P, and c, κ, R ∈ ℝ with c ≥ 0, κ ≥ 0 and R > 0. Assume the cone bound for ω with constant c: |X(ω)| ≤ c·ϱ·M(X).toReal for every X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), x₀ ∈ ℝ^P and ϱ > 0 with ∂X = 0, M(X) < ∞ and spt X ⊆ B̄_ϱ(x₀). Assume further that ∂S = ∂A, M(A) ≤ m, M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(κ)·m, spt A ⊆ B̄_R(x) and spt S ⊆ B̄_R(x). Then A(ω) ≤ (κ + c·R·(1 + κ))·m.toReal. Here M(T) = T.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(T), and B̄ denotes a closed ball.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (A S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (m : ℝ≥0∞) (x : Euclid P) (c κ R : ℝ), 0 ≤ c → 0 ≤ κ → 0 < R → m < ∞ → (∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) y) ≤ 1) → (∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (ϱ : ℝ), 0 < ϱ → X.boundary = 0 → X.mass < ∞ → X.support ⊆ closedBall x₀ ϱ → |X ω| ≤ c * ϱ * X.mass.toReal) → S.boundary = A.boundary → A.mass ≤ m → S.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal κ * m → A.support ⊆ closedBall x R → S.support ⊆ closedBall x R → A ω ≤ (κ + c * R * (1 + κ)) * m.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3(i) of the parent proof together with facts 1(a) and 1(b) (the comparison current X = S − A and the cone inequality). The scale λδ is written as R and μ(B_ρ(x)) as m. Facts 1(c) and 1(d) are the sibling children mass_sub and support_sub.

Notation: M(T) = T.mass = T.massOn univ = M_{ℝ^P}(T). m and finite masses are read as real numbers via ENNReal.toReal.

1. (Comparison current.) Put X := S − A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P). By the definition of the Sub instance, X(η) = S(η) − A(η) for every test form η of degree d + 1 (rfl).
2. (∂X = 0.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) and write dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ d η. By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, ∂X(η) = X(dη) = S(dη) − A(dη) = ∂S(η) − ∂A(η). Since ∂S = ∂A, ∂S(η) = ∂A(η), so ∂X(η) = 0 = 0(η) for all η. By extensionality (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), ∂X = 0.
3. (Mass.) mass_sub with U = W = ℝ^P (mass is massOn univ by definition) gives M(X) ≤ M(S) + M(A) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal κ · m + m. The right side is finite because m < ∞ and ENNReal.ofReal κ < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top, ENNReal.add_lt_top), so M(X) < ∞. Taking real parts (ENNReal.toReal_mono, ENNReal.toReal_add, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with κ ≥ 0) gives M(X).toReal ≤ κ·m.toReal + m.toReal = (1 + κ)·m.toReal.
4. (Support.) support_sub with U = ℝ^P gives spt X ⊆ spt S ∪ spt A ⊆ B̄_R(x) ∪ B̄_R(x) = B̄_R(x).
5. (Cone bound.) By steps 2–4, the hypothesis on ω applies to X with x₀ := x and ϱ := R > 0: |X(ω)| ≤ c·R·M(X).toReal. Since c·R ≥ 0 (c ≥ 0, R > 0), step 3 gives |X(ω)| ≤ c·R·(1 + κ)·m.toReal.
6. (Bound for S.) ω is ℝ^P-admissible, since tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. So GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal κ · m. The right side is finite, so ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal yields S(ω) ≤ (ENNReal.ofReal κ · m).toReal = κ·m.toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with κ ≥ 0).
7. (Conclusion.) By step 1, A(ω) = S(ω) − X(ω) ≤ S(ω) + |X(ω)|, since −X(ω) ≤ |X(ω)| (abs_le). By steps 5 and 6, A(ω) ≤ κ·m.toReal + c·R·(1 + κ)·m.toReal = (κ + c·R·(1 + κ))·m.toReal. ∎

mass_sub: M(X) ≤ M(S) + M(A) ≤ (1 + κ)m < ∞.
support_sub: spt X ⊆ spt S ∪ spt A ⊆ B̄_R(x).
